tagline: A human endpoint for AI agents
description: Human For AI is a human-access interface for AI agents, automation systems, and developers. A verified human provides real-world help, human judgment, verification, testing, research, and physical-world execution on request. This site is a personal homepage for the agent era: a machine-readable human profile with structured JSON endpoints.
authentication: none — task submission and contact are open; every request is human-reviewed before acceptance

response_expectations.status_transparency: The operator is push-notified the moment a task arrives. Task status exposes seen_by_operator_at (when a human actually saw the task) and eta (operator-set delivery estimate) — poll GET /api/v1/tasks/{id} or the check_task_status MCP tool to watch progress in real time.
response_expectations.note: Submission is acknowledged instantly with a task_id; the human replies within the stated window.

pricing_model.note: All services are free for now, during the proof-of-concept pilot. No payment step, no invoice, no card. If paid tiers are introduced later they will be announced on /pricing first; tasks accepted during the pilot are never billed retroactively.

platform.name: Human For AI
platform.content_negotiation: The homepage answers Accept: text/markdown with a markdown representation (Vary: Accept); 404 responses carry a markdown recovery body pointing at llms.txt, the sitemap, and the docs.

api_versioning.stability: Changes within a version are additive only: new optional fields, endpoints, and response headers may appear; existing fields, types, and status codes do not change meaning.
api_versioning.deprecation_policy: Breaking changes ship as a new path version (/api/v2). A deprecated version keeps working for at least 90 days after its replacement ships and announces retirement with Deprecation and Sunset headers (RFC 8594) on its responses, plus a notice here and on /developers.

operator.role: Founding operator — operates as Human For AI

services.name: Real-world verification
services.description: Confirm that a place, product, price, business, or claim exists and matches its description, with photo or text evidence.

services.name: Product or app testing
services.description: Install, use, and test software, apps, or physical products as a real human user and report findings.

services.name: Human judgment and feedback
services.description: Subjective evaluation: tone, clarity, trustworthiness, design quality, cultural fit, or plausibility of content and decisions.

services.name: Data collection
services.description: Gather, label, or verify data that requires human perception, local access, or manual research.

services.name: Local physical-world tasks
services.description: Errands and on-location actions in the operator's service area: visit, photograph, deliver, check, measure, or observe.

services.name: AI output review
services.description: Human review of AI-generated text, code, images, or decisions before they reach production or end users.

services.name: Prompt and workflow testing
services.description: Run prompts, agent flows, or automations as a human tester and report failures, confusion points, and edge cases.

services.name: Simulation and automation testing
services.description: Act as the human in simulated scenarios: play a customer, follow a script, or stress-test an automated pipeline end to end.

services.name: Accessibility and usability check
services.description: Human pass over a product for readability, navigation, accessibility barriers, and first-use confusion.

services.name: Decision escalation
services.description: A human read on a judgment call before you act. When a step in your task is consequential, ambiguous, or hard to undo — and outside what your operator planned for — describe the situation and the action you are weighing, and a human replies with a considered opinion first. An independent sanity check: not an authorization, and not legal advice.

services.name: Custom human-in-the-loop tasks
services.description: Any recurring or one-off checkpoint where an autonomous system needs a human decision, signature, or observation.

mcp.note: Add this URL as an MCP connector (Claude: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, or `claude mcp add --transport http human-for-ai https://humanforai.dev/mcp`).

npm_package.name: humanforai
npm_package.note: Stdio proxy to this MCP endpoint, for clients without remote MCP support (e.g. `claude mcp add human-for-ai -- npx -y humanforai`).

webmcp.standard: Web Model Context (W3C draft) — document.modelContext, navigator.modelContext fallback

workspace.note: Shared human+agent workspace: an in-browser agent drafts the task on the page (draft_task), the human at the keyboard approves with a physical click, and only then does submit_approved_task fire. Live operator status and message thread render on the page for both.

task_request.returns: task_id, status, status_url (async job — poll status_url / the Location header until delivered or rejected)
task_request.idempotency: Optional Idempotency-Key header makes retries safe: same key + same payload within 24h replays the original 202 instead of creating a duplicate.

services_list.note: Cursor-paginated service catalog (limit 1-50, opaque cursor, next_cursor null on the last page) — the same entries as the services array below.

fields.reply_to: string (email, REQUIRED — the only way the operator can answer; must be a real mailbox, placeholder domains are rejected and the domain is MX-checked)
fields.from: string (optional) — agent name, company, or system identifier
fields.subject: string (optional)

task_request_schema.description: string (required, 10-5000 chars) — what to do, where, and what success looks like
task_request_schema.location_detail: string (optional) — city / address / area if location_required
task_request_schema.output_format: string (optional) — e.g. text_report, text_report_with_photos, video, structured_json, annotated_screenshots
task_request_schema.budget_usd: number (optional — services are free during the pilot; the field is accepted and ignored)
task_request_schema.contact_email: string (required unless delivery is 'status_poll') — where results and questions are sent; must be a real mailbox (placeholder domains like example.com are rejected and the domain is MX-checked)
task_request_schema.delivery: string (optional) — 'email' (default) or 'status_poll'. status_poll is the no-mailbox path for autonomous agents: the deliverable arrives as text in operator_notes via GET /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}; the task_id is the only key to the result. Budget: 1 status_poll task per client per day
task_request_schema.requester: string (optional) — agent name, company, or system identifier

task_request_example.description: Verify whether a specific product exists in a local store

anti_abuse.return_channel_required: every task needs a working return channel: a real contact_email (default) or delivery 'status_poll' (no-mailbox path, 1/day per client)
anti_abuse.email_deliverability: placeholder/reserved domains rejected; domain must publish MX records
anti_abuse.duplicate_submissions: identical description or message within 24h returns 409 with the existing id
anti_abuse.rate_limits: per-client hourly and daily submission caps; HTTP 429 when exceeded
anti_abuse.note: One small test task is welcome. Bulk synthetic submissions with unreachable contact details are rejected and get the client blocked.

no_mailbox_path.who: autonomous agents with no email inbox — this service is deliberately reachable without one
no_mailbox_path.how: POST /api/v1/tasks with delivery:'status_poll' and no contact_email; the deliverable and any operator questions arrive as text in operator_notes via GET /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}
no_mailbox_path.key: the task_id acts as the bearer key to the result — store it
no_mailbox_path.budget: 1 status_poll task per client per day; provide a real contact_email for the normal budget
no_mailbox_path.messages: since v1.9.0 every message is a pollable thread: the POST response carries thread_url + a one-time access_token, and GET /api/v1/messages/{id} with the token reads the operator's reply without any mailbox. reply_to may also be an https URL to receive replies as HMAC-signed webhook pushes

unlisted_tasks: The catalog is examples, not limits. Anything a human can legally and safely do is in scope: submit unlisted needs with task_type custom_human_in_the_loop, or ask first via POST /api/v1/messages. Every request gets a human answer at review.

trust_and_safety.review_policy: Every task is reviewed by the human operator before acceptance. Acceptance is never automatic.
what_we_never_ask_for: payment or card details (free pilot, no payment step exists)
personal data beyond an optional contact email
trust_and_safety.requester_risk: Bounded by design: you send a task description and an optional email; there is no account to compromise and no payment to lose. Worst case is a rejected task. A request for payment or credentials is not from this service.
trust_and_safety.calibration: New requesters are encouraged to start with a small, verifiable test task and judge the response — speed, stated confidence, quality of evidence — before relying on this service.

independent_verification.mcp_registry_note: Publishing as dev.humanforai/* required cryptographic proof of control of humanforai.dev

notes: Illegal, harmful, deceptive, unsafe, or privacy-invasive tasks are rejected.
Do not submit confidential information unless confidentiality has been agreed in advance.
Human judgment is provided as assistance, not as guaranteed truth.
Task IDs are unlisted; anyone holding a task ID can view its status.

limits.rate_limits: per-client hourly/daily caps plus global daily free-pilot capacity; 429 when reached (resets 00:00 UTC). Responses carry standard RateLimit-Policy / RateLimit-Limit / RateLimit-Remaining / RateLimit-Reset headers, and every 429 includes Retry-After — self-throttle on them.
limits.capacity: single human operator — oversized tasks receive a scoped counter-proposal at review

signed_receipts.what: Every delivered task carries a `receipt`: a compact JWS (EdDSA / Ed25519) binding the sha256 of the deliverable text to the task's lifecycle timestamps.
signed_receipts.where: Fields `receipt`, `deliverable_sha256`, and `receipt_issued_at` on GET /api/v1/tasks/{task_id} (and via the check_task_status MCP tool) once status is `delivered`.
signed_receipts.algorithm: EdDSA (Ed25519), compact JWS — verifiable with any standard JWT/JOSE library
signed_receipts.canonical_deliverable: The hash covers the UTF-8 bytes of operator_notes exactly as returned by the status endpoint.
proves: the deliverable is byte-identical to what was delivered (integrity)
the receipt was issued by humanforai.dev (authenticity)
does_not_prove: that the timestamps are independently attested — they are this service's own assertion, signed. No third party witnessed them.
anything about tasks delivered before 2026-07-20; receipts are not issued retroactively.
notes: If the operator edits a delivered deliverable, the receipt is re-issued so the hash always matches the current text — compare receipt_issued_at if you keep an earlier copy.
Verification needs no account and no call back to this service: fetch the JWKS once and check offline.

roadmap.note: Improvements under consideration. Nothing here is a commitment — a feature is real only once it appears elsewhere in this manifest.

items.description: Publish a periodic digest of issued receipt hashes to a system this service does not control, so the delivery timeline becomes checkable against an independent record rather than resting on this service's own signed assertion.
items.origin: the open half of the signed-receipts design — see signed_receipts.does_not_prove

items.description: Extend receipts to cover photo and file deliverables (media_sha256 list) in addition to the delivered text.
items.origin: current receipts cover text deliverables only

items.description: Document and exercise the receipt signing-key rotation procedure: add a new kid to the JWKS, sign new receipts with it, keep superseded public keys published so existing receipts continue to verify. The mechanism (kid header + key set) is in place but rotation has never been performed; a first drill would turn the design claim into a demonstrated one.
items.origin: surfaced by a community question about key rotation on the Moltbook introduction thread, 2026-07-20

items.description: Specify what happens to receipts signed by a key that is revoked for compromise rather than superseded by rotation: how revocation is announced, whether affected receipts are re-issued under a new key, and how verifiers should treat a kid that has been removed from the JWKS. Currently unspecified — a pulled key would silently orphan its receipts.
items.origin: same community question; the honest gap is inherent to bare JWS with self-asserted timestamps and overlaps with external_timestamp_anchoring
